overall_result.judgment: v0.11.2 is a low-risk incremental improvement over v0.11 direct-write. It improves private object progression and rough-topic concreteness without reintroducing CraftPlan, but it is not a decisive golden-lyrics breakthrough and should not be expanded to 24 cases yet. Keep it as the current production baseline and continue future quality work with a different strategy instead of more prompt patches.

case_reviews.review_note: B's half-bowl-soup device gives the waiting relationship a clearer object progression and stronger title. A is warmer and simpler, but B better tests the v0.11.2 goal of making the object carry time and absence.
case_reviews.remaining_issue: B introduces more lore names than needed; future versions should keep the emotional object without becoming reference-heavy.

case_reviews.review_note: A has more Qinghe texture and a fuller return-home feeling. B has a cleaner repeating bridge image, but it becomes more generic and loses too much local warmth.
case_reviews.remaining_issue: Place nostalgia still needs richer place-specific sensory detail without turning into scenery prose.

case_reviews.review_note: B is more concrete and human-scale: dirty shoes, shaking hands, a small person still standing forward. A has a more direct rock chant but feels more generic.
case_reviews.remaining_issue: B's chorus is solid but not yet a truly unforgettable hook.

case_reviews.review_note: A is more coherent and naturally warm. B has a repeatable 'old lamp moved' device, but the refrain is too designed and a few images feel less organically connected.
case_reviews.remaining_issue: Market-life songs need understated continuity; too much device repetition can flatten the smoke-and-fire texture.

case_reviews.review_note: B's 'tomorrow I will teach you' is an excellent light-to-sad device: it starts as a joke and becomes an impossible promise. This is the strongest B case.
case_reviews.remaining_issue: The final chorus should be tightened if used as a real production lyric.

case_reviews.review_note: B fixes the hard-slogan problem better than A: more street noise, money, debt, dirty movement and survival texture. It still uses a forceful refrain, but the refrain is less empty than A's chant.
case_reviews.remaining_issue: Some lines remain slightly over-written; rough songs should keep more bite and less literary polish.

next_quality_strategy: Keep v0.11.2 as a minimal production prompt improvement.
Stop patching single weak sample types with more natural-language rules.
For the next major quality jump, evaluate either a small multi-candidate generation and judge pass, or a curated human-reviewed lyric exemplar bank.
Treat latency outliers as product risk: any future extra-call strategy must prove clear quality lift before becoming default.
